QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_23

question.text: Amit invested Rs.1,00,000 in a fund that delivered 40% return over 6 years. What is the simple annualized return?

explanation.text: The Logic: Simple annualized return = Total return / Number of years = 40% / 6 = 6.67% per annum. For horizons over one year, the CAGR for the same data is ((1.40)^(1/6)) - 1, about 5.77%, which is lower because of compounding. The Trap: Option B (40.00%) is the total cumulative return, not the annualized figure. Option C (8.00%) does not follow from any standard return formula on the inputs. Option D (5.77%) is the CAGR, not the simple annualized return the question asks for. Note: Distributor/pro-tip wording removed; explanation kept to the simple annualization calculation with an optional CAGR contrast in neutral wording.
